question.problem:
Let $X$ be a random variable with the probability density function shown below. What are the modes of $X?$

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{x(6-x)^{2}}{128}, & 0\le x\le 8 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
The modes of a random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ are the values of $x$ at the global maxima of $f(x).$

To find the global maxima of $f(x),$ we find the critical points of $f(x)$ and then apply the candidates test.

First, we find the critical points.

- The piece of $f(x)$ defined on $0\le x\le 8$ is $f(x)=\frac{x(6-x)^{2}}{128}.$ Taking the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{(6-x)^{2}-2x(6-x)}{128} \\  & =\frac{(6-x)(6-x-2x)}{128} \\  & =\frac{3(6-x)(2-x)}{128},\end{aligned}
$$

and solving ${f}^{′}(x)=0,$ we get

$$
\frac{3(6-x)(2-x)}{128}\,⟹\,x=2,6.
$$

All of these critical points are within the interval $[0,8],$ so we keep them all.

- The derivative doesn't exist at the endpoints $x=0,8.$ So, these are critical points as well.

Now, we evaluate $f(x)$ at the critical points $x=0,2,6,8:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0) & =\frac{0(6-0)^{2}}{128}=0 \\ f(2) & =\frac{2(6-2)^{2}}{128}=\frac{1}{4} \\ f(6) & =\frac{6(6-6)^{2}}{128}=0 \\ f(8) & =\frac{8(6-8)^{2}}{128}=\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we compare all of the values above. The largest values are

$$
f(2)=f(8)=\frac{1}{4}.
$$

Therefore, the modes of $X$ are $2$ and $8.$
